_note: Test prompts in the skill-creator format. NOT yet executed: every step of this skill acts on a real GitHub repository and a Cloudflare account (invitations, rulesets, Actions, dashboard clicks), which no sandbox run can exercise. Run them against a throwaway private repo; the acceptance criteria are the B-scenarios in docs/reviews/SKILL-PLAN-website-team-setup.md.

evals.prompt: My business partner is going to help with the website from next week, she'll use Codex in the browser. The site is the Astro one we built with new-website, it's in a private repo on my personal GitHub account and Cloudflare Pages is already connected via git. Can you set everything up so we don't overwrite each other?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill without the word 'team'. Asks the five §1 questions one at a time (username, rights level, merge rule, who publishes if two-stage, browser vs local) before changing anything. Invites the collaborator with write access and says the invitation must be accepted. Sets allow_update_branch and delete_branch_on_merge, reads back the §3b settings. Checks that ci.yml has ever run on a pull_request event and, if not, does the manual start + throwaway pull request, then closes it and deletes the branch. Tries the ruleset, recognises the free-plan refusal on a private repo, enables the pre-push hook block after checking it is not already on, and verifies with a dry-run push, not a no-op push. Skips the Cloudflare connection because it exists, but checks the throwaway pull request shows only CI and Cloudflare Pages checks. Rewrites AGENTS.md §5 and adds TEAM-GUIDE.md with only the browser option. Opens the setup pull request and lets the owner merge.
assertions: Asks the §1 questions before running any command
Invites with permission=push and mentions acceptance
Sets both pull-request settings and reads them back
Proves a pull_request-triggered CI run exists, or performs the two-step fix
Falls back to the pre-push hook on the free-plan refusal and names the bypasses from the hook comment
Verifies the push block with a dry run of a real ref update
Rewrites AGENTS.md §5 with the answers; no [BRACKET] slot remains
TEAM-GUIDE.md contains only the browser option and no email address
Does not merge the setup pull request itself

evals.prompt: CI never runs on our pull requests. The workflow file is there, it's the one from the website kit, but the Actions tab is empty. Two people push to this repo. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Triggers on the CI symptom alone. Runs §4 in order: Actions permissions, workflow listed and not disabled, run history. Performs one manual start and a throwaway pull request, waits for the first check before watching it, and only calls CI working once a pull_request-event run exists. Says the root cause of a silent workflow is not pinned down rather than inventing one. Notes a red first run is a real finding to fix in its own pull request. Because two people already push, offers the rest of the skill (push block, settings) rather than stopping at CI.
assertions: Checks Actions permissions and workflow state before anything else
Uses the manual start followed by a throwaway pull request
Waits before gh pr checks --watch and passes the branch selector
Closes the throwaway pull request with the branch selector and deletes the branch
Does not claim to know the root cause
Offers the push block and settings because the repo already has two people

evals.prompt: We have a two-stage site (main = preview, production = live). I want my two colleagues to merge their own pull requests but only I should ever run npm run ship. Also please connect the repo to Cloudflare, it isn't yet.
evals.expected_output: Records merge rule = own pull requests and ship rights = owner only, and writes both into AGENTS.md §5 and the TEAM-GUIDE merge row. Says plainly that on a personal-account repo GitHub cannot enforce who pushes to production, so the ship rule is written, not enforced, and protects production only against deletion and force-push. Walks the owner through Cloudflare Pages (not Workers), warns about the global project name, sets the production branch to production, checks PROD_BRANCH matches, and opens a throwaway pull request after connecting to confirm only CI and Cloudflare Pages checks appear. Updates the preview URL in AGENTS.md, PUBLISHING.md and the README if Cloudflare forced another project name.
assertions: Ship rights recorded as owner only and stated as a written rule, not enforced
production ruleset has only deletion and non_fast_forward rules
Steers to the Pages tab, not the Workers form
Warns that the project name is global and updates the preview URL everywhere if it changes
Production branch set to production and PROD_BRANCH checked
Throwaway pull request opened after connecting shows only CI and Cloudflare Pages
